From e0da8a8cac74f4b9f577979d131f0d2b88a84487 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Ziqing Chen <chenziqing@xiaomi.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 21:24:37 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] ALSA: control: Validate buf_len before strnlen() in
 snd_ctl_elem_init_enum_names()

snd_ctl_elem_init_enum_names() advances pointer p through the names
buffer while decrementing buf_len. If buf_len reaches zero but items
remain, the next iteration calls strnlen(p, 0).

While strnlen(p, 0) returns 0 and would hit the existing name_len == 0
error path, CONFIG_FORTIFY_SOURCE's fortified strnlen() first checks
maxlen against __builtin_dynamic_object_size(). When Clang loses track
of p's object size inside the loop, this triggers a BRK exception panic
before the return value is examined.

Add a buf_len == 0 guard at the loop entry to prevent calling fortified
strnlen() on an exhausted buffer.

Found by kernel fuzz testing through Xiaomi Smartphone.

Fixes: 8d448162bda5 ("ALSA: control: add support for ENUMERATED user space controls")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Ziqing Chen <chenziqing@xiaomi.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260414132437.261304-1-chenziqing@xiaomi.com
Signed-off-by: Takashi Iwai <tiwai@suse.de>

diff --git a/sound/core/control.c b/sound/core/control.c
index 374e703d15a9..5e51857635e6 100644
--- a/sound/core/control.c
+++ b/sound/core/control.c
@@ -1648,6 +1648,10 @@ static int snd_ctl_elem_init_enum_names(struct user_element *ue)
 	/* check that there are enough valid names */
 	p = names;
 	for (i = 0; i < ue->info.value.enumerated.items; ++i) {
+		if (buf_len == 0) {
+			kvfree(names);
+			return -EINVAL;
+		}
 		name_len = strnlen(p, buf_len);
 		if (name_len == 0 || name_len >= 64 || name_len == buf_len) {
 			kvfree(names);
-- 
2.34.1

### Summary of the Patch

#### Modifications in each file

- **`sound/core/control.c`**: In the function `snd_ctl_elem_init_enum_names()`, a guard condition is added at the entry of the loop that iterates over the names buffer. The new code checks if `buf_len` has reached zero; if so, it frees the allocated buffer and returns `-EINVAL` immediately, avoiding any further calls to `strnlen()` with a zero `maxlen` parameter.

#### Relationships between changes

- The change is confined to a single file and addresses a specific vulnerability in the loop logic. The original code decremented `buf_len` while advancing a pointer through the names buffer, but did not check for `buf_len == 0` before calling `strnlen()`. When `buf_len` became zero, `strnlen(p, 0)` would be invoked, which is harmless in standard C but triggers a panic under `CONFIG_FORTIFY_SOURCE` because the fortified wrapper verifies `maxlen` against the object size (which may become unknown after pointer arithmetic). Adding the early check ensures that `strnlen()` is never called with a zero `maxlen` when the buffer is exhausted, preventing the crash while maintaining the intended validation of the input.
